result.title: Similar Is Not Useful: Selecting In-Context Demonstrations by Closed-Loop Utility
result.summary: Retrieval-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies fill their context with the demonstrations whose frames look most like the current observation under frozen DINOv2 embeddings. We ask whether visual similarity selects the demonstrations that make the policy succeed. For a frozen retrieval-augmented VLA (RICL on $π_0$-FAST, LIBERO), we make the demonstration pool swappable at run time and score each demonstration's utility by regressing the closed-loop success of 60 fixed-size pools on their membership. On initial states disjoint from those used for scoring, pools of the five highest-utility demonstrations succeed on 66.4% of 760 paired episodes across 19 tasks, pools of the five most similar on 55.7%, and random pools on 55.5%. Utility beats similarity by 10.8 points ($p=3.2\times10^{-6}$; positive on 15 of 18 untied tasks), including on 12 tasks the policy was never primed on, and similarity-selected pools do no better than random ($+0.1$ points). Within a task, a pool's visual similarity to the test scenes tracks its success at Spearman 0.10; across tasks, similarity separates tasks whose scenes differ and falls to chance when two tasks share a scene. The gain comes from on-task closed-loop evidence: best-of-ten direct search over pools recovers two-thirds of it with 100 rollouts. Against the shipped 20-demonstration pool, utility-curated pools of five lead by 7.0 points over 560 paired episodes from two evaluation runs ($p=0.006$), and utility-ordered retrieval inside the full pool leads by 4.5 points ($p=0.055$).

AI.brief_summary: 论文检验「视觉相似」是否等于「有用」：在冻结的检索增强 VLA 上让示范池可在运行时替换，用 60 个固定池的闭环成功率回归出各示范的效用，并比较高效用池、最相似池与随机池的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接给出「相似不等于有用」的量化证据，与视觉证据筛选、以及嵌入相似度能否承载任务必要信息的问题相通；其闭环效用打分可供核查是否能迁移到推理期的证据或示范选择。
